The personal tier's version of the orphan flag is attention drift: *"this week's
sessions were 70% in skills repos — nothing there links to your stated focus."*
That sentence requires knowing where time went, and there are two ways to know:

- **Ledger writes only.** Count entries created per ledger. Zero new data collected,
  nothing to leak. But it measures *capture*, not attention — a week of deep work
  that produced two decisions looks quieter than an hour of thrashing that produced
  nine.
- **Session metadata.** Read session start/stop and cwd from the agent harness.
  Genuinely measures where time went. But dira begins recording a log of the user's
  working behaviour, which is a materially different privacy proposition for a tool
  that also holds their private strategy — and it is the kind of feature that is
  easy to add and impossible to un-ship.

There is a third option worth weighing: **don't build it.** Attention drift is the
one proposed feature that is closer to self-surveillance than to navigation, and
int-0003's subtractive discipline argues against it. A compass that reports your
bearing is useful; one that grades your effort is a different product.

Not blocking anything — the personal tier ships without drift detection. Defer until
the tier has been used long enough to know whether the mirror is actually wanted.
